video_title: SGA has NO CHOICE but to go 'NUCLEAR' in Game 5 - Chiney | Get Up

quotes.speaker: James Harden
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden on Cavaliers' series loss to Knicks
quotes.excerpt: obviously they just they dominated us for O, but I don't know if I can necessarily answer that question
quotes.quote: You know, obviously they just they dominated us for O, but um yeah, I don't know I don't know if I can necessarily answer that question. Just because genuinely I do feel like we we are we are the better team.

quotes.speaker: Chiney Ogwumike
quotes.summary_phrase: Chiney Ogwumike on Harden's claim of being the better team
quotes.excerpt: in my soul, there's no way you can say your team is a better team when you get swept
quotes.quote: Out of anyone on this network, I am probably the biggest James Harden apologist because I am from Houston, Texas where he became an MVP and was extremely dominant. But in my soul, there's no way you can say you're the better team or your team is a better team when you get swept and the manner in which you got swept. And it's unfortunate and on top of it to say it when you know that in this series, you left much to be desired, that's tough. They were not the better team. And it was proven handily. And so I have a tough time agreeing. Now, when we go into games, we tell ourselves that, but after games, we have to face the reality and hear the music. And the music was loud. The music was a symphony. And so I can't agree, I understand the mentality, but at the end of the day, ball don't lie and it it it really bounces in New York's favor.

quotes.speaker: Jay Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Williams on James Harden's indifference to public opinion
quotes.excerpt: I don't think James Harden is worried about what anybody thinks about James Harden
quotes.quote: I just, you know, when I hear James talk, I I feel like I I know what it is. And I I I don't think James Harden is worried about what anybody thinks about James Harden. And I don't think anything that James Harden can say is going to change somebody's interpretation of James Harden. If you think James Harden plays a style of losing basketball, then you're going to feel that way. You're going to feel that way it's going to be confirmed after this series. There was a part of me as a former player, even Donovan Mitchell's comments as well when he backed James Harden up. At some point, you got to be in the trenches in the Foxhole together. The rest of the world doesn't have to believe you, but you got to fight for each other. And if James Harden is coming back next year, I'm not saying what he said is right because it's not on paper when we listen to it. But in that locker room, if you're coming back to that team, you want your teammates to believe in you and what you have to do the following year. And Donovan Mitchell felt the same way when he backed up James Harden in his post presser too.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Cavaliers' future and LeBron James speculation
quotes.excerpt: The Cavs could only pay him $3 million as they're currently constructed
quotes.quote: Yeah, they have two pathways they can go. One they can sort of run this team back, maybe change Kenny Atkinson's coaching staff, go through a training camp similar to what the Knicks did. Basically say we believe in this team and keep it going. Two, they could make major changes. They already made a major Harden trade, trading away one of their young All-Stars, Darius Garland. They could examine trading away one of their other young players, either Jared Allen or Evan Mobley, which would be a major move. And when I was walking out on the court last night as the Cavs fans were all yielding their arena to the Knicks fans, every single Cavs fan that passed me said, are we getting LeBron? Are we getting LeBron? The Cavs could only pay him $3 million as they're currently constructed. They could make moves to try to attract him, to try to trade for him. But those would be complex, but LeBron James will be an unrestricted free agent in a month.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Thunder's offensive struggles and injuries
quotes.excerpt: This time, however, their challenge is to fix their offense because they're missing their offensive creators
quotes.quote: Well, obviously Oklahoma City is at home. They have been brilliant on their home court, the last two playoff runs and they've also been excellent problem solvers. When they've had challenges in the playoffs, the last couple of years, they have always bounced back. This time, however, their challenge is to fix their offense because they're missing their offensive creators outside Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. AJ Mitchell will be out tonight with a calf injury and look, calf strains Greeny are typically measured in weeks. This is late in the season, you don't know but I don't know if they're going to get him back in this series. Jalen Williams they have had to show their hand a little bit and they've stopped saying hamstring soreness. They have now changed it to hamstring strain. That will be the fourth different hamstring strain he's experienced this year, but he is questionable and he did play a little bit early here after the injury so he's closer. But Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is shooting under 40% in this series. Two lead guards with him are injured. This is a problem for the home team tonight.

quotes.speaker: Chiney Ogwumike
quotes.summary_phrase: Chiney Ogwumike on Victor Wembanyama's future MVP potential
quotes.excerpt: You have someone that is a future MVP learning his star power in real time on the fly
quotes.quote: You mentioned monster in your conference. This is a monster for the league for the years to come. You have someone that is a future MVP learning his star power in real time on the fly and Victor Wembanyama. This leads me to the conclusion that SGA has no choice but to go nuclear. He has to take the shots. It's going to be difficult. AJ Mitchell, J-Dub, the secondary and tertiary, I know that's third, um, creators, right on a squad. His only choice is to do battle by himself. And he we've seen him do it. He did it last year in the NBA finals. Remember, the Pacers were the hottest offense and then he realized I have to shoot the ball 20 times in the first half to be aggressive for my team to play aggressive for it to be contagious. We saw him do it versus the Phoenix Suns. Down J-Dub, he comes in, drops 40. And then the shots look better for his teammates. But I'll say this, he's the back-to-back MVP, it's not going to be easy. 14 out of his 15 shots where he was 6 for 15, were contested. He was double-teamed 11 times. He is the man with the trophy and he will have to play like it.

quotes.speaker: Jay Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Williams on SGA's opportunity to elevate his game
quotes.excerpt: This is when the greatest players grab on that mantle and say, no, okay. It's time
quotes.quote: Greatness is never easy. And both you and Wendy may mention of the problem for us. No, this is an opportunity. This is an opportunity for SGA. You're at home, defending World Champions, you're down two ball handlers. This is when the greatest players grab on that mantle and say, no, okay. It's time. And what have all the conversations been about about whether it's inflaming into the free throw line, all that stuff does not matter. It matters about this moment. And I know it's never one player versus five, but we to talk about the best players in the game of basketball can they elevate their level of play and the players around them in the biggest moments. And this is a massive moment for SGA. And that's okay to say.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Knicks' historic 11-game playoff run
quotes.excerpt: It's one of the greatest most dominant 11-game runs in the history of the league
quotes.quote: Yeah, it's one of the greatest uh most dominant 11-game runs in the history of the league, regular season, post-season, whatever you want to say. You beat opponents in the post-season. That's how you decide who wins the series. You break opponents in the post-season. But they've gotten their opponents to quit. In these close-out games by the end of these series after facing the Knicks for a run, they quit. They're done. They've done it. And they do it in the first quarter. All three of those close-out games, they've ended the game by the end of the first quarter. This is desperation time. You're in your close-out. This is about pride and all that stuff. They get them to quit. The Cavs stopped running and they stopped jumping. There's no other way to define quitting. And that happened because the Knicks were so much more dominant than them.

quotes.speaker: Jay Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Williams on Knicks' championship mentality and focus
quotes.excerpt: I do not care about Atlanta. I do not care about Philly. I do not care about the Cavs
quotes.quote: Job not done. I do not care about Atlanta. I do not care about Philly. I do not care about the Cavs. I do not care about what people think about the Eastern Conference if it's weak enough. I care that we're healthy and we're ready to go to battle. And our war paint is on our faces when we go to the NBA championship. And that was the demeanor that you saw from a championship contending team last night. Everybody else wants to party. Look at the faces of Jalen Brunson or look at Karl-Anthony Towns. This team is on a mission. And I think it's all fair to say, guys, if the Spurs and OKC go to it's going to game six regardless. If it goes to a game seven, if they can be healthy, have their legs ready, they have their best chance to win a championship.

quotes.speaker: Alan Hahn
quotes.summary_phrase: Alan Hahn on Knicks' Matrix-like team basketball and trust
quotes.excerpt: They've been the best team in NBA history. Over the 11-game stretch that has ensued from that moment
quotes.quote: Well, so so take me to the the actual because you're you give me some analytics here. Not not analytics. Give me some analysis here, okay? I'm hosting round one of the NFL Draft on Thursday night, April 23rd in Pittsburgh. And my Knicks group chat is exploding with the Knicks lose a one-point game in Atlanta. They go down 2-1. Mikal Bridges sucks and we got to change everything and the Knicks are going to lose and they're giving me a heart attack and all of that. From that point forward, they've been, this is not an exaggeration. This is not hyperbole. They've been the best team in NBA history. Over over the 11-game stretch that has ensued from and ensued from that moment, they have played better than any team has ever played in any 11 games in the entire history of the NBA. You don't just do that by diving on loose balls. How have they done it? By reconfiguring their value system. And I know you can speak to this as well. Understanding that Jalen Brunson is the closer. He also will get you started, but really at the end of the game, he will deliver. Karl-Anthony Towns is capable of more. We thought that hey, this was a guy that knocked down threes, he will get to the post. We were having crisis management conversations because he did not get enough touches. Finally, they trusted in him and listened to him and he's backed it up. He has had two triple-doubles in this postseason. Small tight tweaks on the fringes. They have trusted their guys. Mikal Bridges despite going through droughts in the season, we need you to knock down that open corner three. He's done it. They brought in energy boosters. They finally got the the help off the bench. It all starts with trusting and also doing things a little bit differently. And I know you can speak to that. Well, I I I watched them again every single game very, very closely and watching what they've done over this 11-game stretch. It reminds me of the Matrix. When Neo finally started seeing the ones and the zeros. And and that's that's what it looks like. I mean, they're just making passes like it's all connected all at one time. But it came together. It's it's it's team basketball. Which is what's celebrated in this town more than ever because the teams that did win championships, think about it. It's something it's a great Bill Bradley said this about those teams back then. We didn't have the best players in the league on our team. We had the best team. And the Knicks for years chased stars. Always trying to get LeBron James, always trying to get Kevin Durant. Give me the biggest name I can get, put him on the stage. And instead they built this team with a second-round pick that nobody really knew much about and Jalen Brunson. They built it that way, became a team, but it took time to get there. That's the most important part. And I think that's what's as admirable about this team as anything. But it's funny because the Matrix came out by the way in 1999. Last time the Knicks were in the finals.
